title: Rangeland vegetation cover (RAP / rangeland-s2)
description: Rangeland vegetation-cover estimates from the Rangeland Analysis Platform (NTSG, University of Montana), aggregated to H3 resolution 10 as GeoParquet-style hex layers and provided as cloud-optimized GeoTIFFs. Covers annual and perennial forb and grass cover across the contiguous US, plus sagebrush and invasive annual grass cover across the western US.

readme:
## README.md
# public-rap — rangeland vegetation cover

Rangeland vegetation-cover products from NTSG at the University of Montana, aggregated to H3.
Everything here is licensed **CC0 1.0 Universal** (public domain dedication) by the producers;
please cite Allred et al. (2021), <https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.13564>.

## Collections

Two different upstream products live in this bucket, and they do **not** cover the same area.

| collection | variable | extent | source product |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rap-afg-cover` | annual forb & grass cover, % | CONUS | RAP Vegetation Cover v3, band 1 |
| `rap-pfg-cover` | perennial forb & grass cover, % | CONUS | RAP Vegetation Cover v3, band 4 |
| `rap-arte` | sagebrush (*Artemisia*) cover, % | western US | rangeland-s2, UTM zones 10–13 |
| `rap-iag` | invasive annual grass cover, % | western US | rangeland-s2, UTM zones 10–13 |

**Annual vs perennial.** Annual forbs and grasses include invasive annuals such as cheatgrass;
perennial forbs and grasses are the native perennial herbaceous cover that invasion tends to
displace. The two are close to ecological opposites, so check which one you are reading.

**The two extents differ.** `rap-afg-cover` and `rap-pfg-cover` cover the conterminous United
States (6 h0 partitions). `rap-arte` and `rap-iag` come from a 10 m Sentinel-2 product published
only for UTM zones 10–13, so they cover the western US out to about 101° W (4 h0 partitions) and
have no data further east. An empty result east of that line is the product's extent, not a gap.

**Suitability.** The producers note these estimates are produced across a broad region but are
primarily intended for rangeland ecosystems, and may be less reliable in other ecosystems such as
forests and agricultural land.

## Query the hex layers with DuckDB

Each collection has one row per H3 cell at resolution 10, holding the area-weighted mean percent
cover. Parent columns `h9`, `h8` and `h0` are present for rollups and joins; `h8` is the resolution
shared with the rest of the catalog.

```sql
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
INSTALL h3 FROM community; LOAD h3;

-- Mean annual forb & grass cover by resolution-8 cell over one partition.
-- Weight by cell area: H3 cells are not equal-area, so a plain AVG is biased.
SELECT h8,
       SUM(afg * h3_cell_area(h10, 'km^2')) / SUM(h3_cell_area(h10, 'km^2')) AS mean_afg
FROM read_parquet(
  'https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-rap/rap-afg-cover/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet',
  hive_partitioning = true)
WHERE h0 = 577199624117288959
GROUP BY h8;
```

Compare the two vegetation-cover variables cell by cell:

```sql
SELECT a.h8,
       AVG(a.afg) AS annual,
       AVG(p.pfg) AS perennial
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-rap/rap-afg-cover/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet') a
JOIN read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-rap/rap-pfg-cover/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet') p
  USING (h10)
GROUP BY a.h8;
```

## Display the COGs in MapLibre GL JS

These are single-band rasters, so they render as a raster source through TiTiler with a colormap.
There is no PMTiles layer and therefore no `source-layer` to set.

```js
const cog = 'https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-rap/rap-afg-cover-cog.tif';

map.addSource('rap-afg', {
  type: 'raster',
  tiles: [
    'https://titiler.nrp-nautilus.io/cog/tiles/WebMercatorQuad/{z}/{x}/{y}.png' +
    `?url=${encodeURIComponent(cog)}&colormap_name=viridis&rescale=0,100`
  ],
  tileSize: 256,
});

map.addLayer({
  id: 'rap-afg',
  type: 'raster',
  source: 'rap-afg',
  paint: { 'raster-opacity': 0.85 },
});
```

Swap the filename for `rap-pfg-cover-cog.tif`, `rap-arte-cog.tif` or `rap-iag-cog.tif` for the other
layers. Values are percent cover from 0 to 100, so `rescale=0,100` is the right range for all four;
255 marks no data and renders transparent.

## Provenance

`raw/` holds the staged upstream files these layers were built from. Upstream republishes each
annual edition in place at a stable URL with no dated archive, so the staged copies plus their
checksums are the citable record. Access dates, sizes and checksums are recorded in each
collection's STAC description.
